title: Settle-up direction and dead end, group amount edit (mobile + web), move-to-group refresh, iPhone edit keypad

acceptance_criteria.outcome: On mobile, opening settle-up from a balance row or the People tab takes payer, payee and amount from the suggested transfers between the viewer and that member; with no such transfer, nothing can be recorded.

Editing only the amount (or other text) of a manual group expense on mobile saves; the server keeps and rescales the stored payers and split. A single payer's amount follows the edited total when payers or split are changed too.
After a personal expense is moved to a group, the mobile Expenses list and other expense-derived views refresh without a manual reload.
In the iOS personal expense edit sheet, with the number pad open, the header stays on screen and one tap on a visible Save Changes saves.
On web, editing a group expense without changing payers or split saves without redoing the split and leaves the stored split to the server (rescaled for a new amount).

Mobile Settle up (button and own row) never opens a sheet without a payer and payee: outgoing transfers are listed, a single incoming one is pre-filled, several incoming ones ask who paid, none says so.

On mobile, Settle up and group expense edit read a comma or dot as the decimal mark (12,50 is 12.50) and record nothing for text that could be read as a different amount, such as 1,234.50, 1,234 or three decimals; the button, payment links and recorded value agree.

On mobile, one settle-up opening sends each payment at most once: further taps do nothing and the sheet cannot be dismissed while sending; after a timeout, lost connection or 5xx no retry is offered, balances are refetched and the person is asked to check first; settle-up does not open from balances that are refreshing or failed to refresh; an attempt the server rejects can be retried. (The server has no duplicate protection.)
Mobile split and payer fields read a comma as the decimal mark (2,50 is 2.50) and never turn it into a larger number.
Mobile personal expense edit uses the same amount reader as AC-007: 12,50 saves 12.50 and unclear text saves nothing.

Mobile receipt item prices (paid and original), split fields and payer fields read a comma as the decimal mark and still drop minus signs. Text that could be another amount (such as 1,234.50 or 1,000, typed or pasted) stays visible, is flagged, and blocks every save that would use it. A third decimal after a lone dot is not taken, as before.

Mobile recurring amounts (template form, inline edit, run now with a typed amount, and the due prompt) can be typed with a dot or comma decimal; unclear or zero amounts save or run nothing and say why. In the due prompt an empty or zero amount still skips that item.

Switching a mobile split to Exact, Percent or Adjust shows 0, and to Shares 1, for everyone without a value, so no blank is sent; the server refuses a blank value in those types with a clear 400 instead of failing, and stores nothing. Equal splits still ignore values.
